messages.subject: Digit.fixed() : problem with files exported by Meshlab
parts:
Hello everyone,

I need to use the function digit.fixed() with files exported by Meshlab (PLY ASCII, of course) and something weird happened... It doesn't work with my laptop neither with two computers I have access to but it works on an other laptop. The error message I receive when I cannot use the function is:

Error in rgl.material(...) : NAs in foreign function call (arg 2)
In addition: Warning message:
In rgl.material(...) : NAs introduced by coercion

While we didn't change anything to make it work on the other laptop. The problem is I don't have access to that laptop right now...

Does someone has any idea about what's going on here ? Is there any way I could use this function on my laptop ? 

Cheers,

Narimane

messages.author: 06c72fc2e70ccfe4
messages.subject: Re: Digit.fixed() : problem with files exported by Meshlab
parts:
Hi Narimane,

Unless you have a particular reason for digitizing your landmarks in R, the Meshlab "PickPoints" tool allows you to landmark within Meshlab, which I have found to be easier than landmarking in R anyway.  Meshlab's landmark files can then be read into R using the read.mpp() function in the Morpho package.

hope that helps,
Grant

messages.author: 5fd23aea044eb06e
messages.subject: Re: Digit.fixed() : problem with files exported by Meshlab
parts:
This seems to happen when the mesh does not have a suitable material attribute and it occurs with the latest version of RGL.

My solution was to copy the material attributes from the sample data scallop ply to my own mesh

data(scallopPLY)
ply <- scallopPLY$ply
MY_MESH$material <- ply$material
